records.name: The Mom Test Conversational Protocol
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [target customer segment] experiences severe operational inefficiency when [executing specific task]. We will verify this by conducting 12 conversational interviews focusing exclusively on past actions, and consider it validated if at least 8 of 12 respondents independently describe a dedicated, imperfect workaround they used within the last 14 days without prompting.

plan.preparation: Formulate 5 open-ended inquiry prompts anchored strictly in historical occurrences. Strip all references to prospective solutions, business concepts, and hypothetical feature sets.
plan.execution: Conduct 30-minute semi-structured interviews. Anchor discussions in past events using prompts such as: "Walk me through the last time you completed [task]," "How much time or budget did resolving that bottleneck consume?" and "What alternative approaches failed?".
plan.dataCollection: Record the dialogue verbatim. Classify every statement into three categories: historical behavior, stated forward-looking speculation, or emotional frustration. Disregard speculative statements entirely during synthesis.

warning.name: Courtesy Bias
warning.text: When interviewers disclose their product concept, interviewees offer polite affirmations to avoid interpersonal friction, generating an illusion of validation.

records.name: Blank Customer Problem Discovery Interview
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [industry persona] suffers from [critical operational bottleneck]. We will verify this by executing 15 structured problem interviews across 3 distinct sub-verticals, and consider it validated if ≥ 70% of interviewees rank this problem as one of their top two operational challenges for the current fiscal quarter.

plan.preparation: Define the Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) based on observable firmographic attributes. Secure interview access by framing outreach as academic or industrial research rather than commercial solicitation.
plan.execution: Introduce the macro domain and instruct respondents to identify their top 3 operational priorities for the quarter. Observe whether the hypothesized problem surfaces organically without prompting.
plan.dataCollection: Score the problem's organizational urgency on a 1–5 scale based on documented resource allocation, executive visibility, and active software evaluations.

warning.name: Polite Problem Inflation
warning.text: In professional contexts, interviewees frequently lament minor operational inconveniences that they have no budget or mandate to resolve.

records.name: Jobs-to-Be-Done (JTBD) Switch and Forces Interview
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [persona] switches away from [incumbent solution] primarily due to [catalyzing push/pull force]. We will verify this by interviewing 10 individuals who transitioned between solutions within the last 90 days, and consider it validated if ≥ 60% point to the exact same triggering event and emotional crisis point.

plan.preparation: Recruit participants who recently switched products within the category. Construct an inquiry matrix covering the four core forces: Push of the Current Situation, Pull of the New Solution, Habit/Inertia, and Anxiety of Change.
plan.execution: Interrogate the chronological arc of the transition: First Thought, Active Looking, Deciding, and Consuming. Inquire: "Where were you when you decided the prior solution was untenable?" "What almost prevented you from finalizing the purchase?"
plan.dataCollection: Map the active forces onto a Cartesian matrix, separating push mechanisms from unvalidated feature wishlists.

warning.name: Post-Hoc Rationalization
warning.text: Consumers routinely construct coherent, rational narratives for purchasing decisions that were fundamentally driven by emotional, impulsive, or organizational impulses.

records.name: Ethnographic Contextual Inquiry (Shadowing)
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [operators] face unrecorded cognitive overload while [operating system X]. We will verify this by observing 6 operators in their natural workplace for 4 hours each, and consider it validated if we record ≥ 5 unprompted compensatory mechanisms (e.g., sticky notes, personal spreadsheets, ad-hoc scripts) per operator per shift.

plan.preparation: Execute confidentiality agreements and workplace access protocols. Construct an observation ledger focused on micro-interruptions, non-verbal cues, and application-switching frequency.
plan.execution: Observe the operator silently during regular shifts. Interrupt only when an operational deviation occurs: "I observed you copied that string into an external editor before pasting it. What motivated that step?"
plan.dataCollection: Compile a minute-by-minute workflow trace logging application switches, error recovery efforts, physical movements, and environmental distractions.

warning.name: Hawthorne Effect
warning.text: Subjects alter their conventional workflows, adhere more strictly to formal protocols, or tidy operational workarounds simply because they are being observed.

records.name: Value Proposition Canvas Customer Profiling
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [customer segment] considers [pain point Y] significantly more critical than [pain point Z]. We will verify this by conducting 10 canvas alignment exercises, and consider it validated if ≥ 75% of participants independently cluster their top 3 jobs and pains into identical operational nodes.

plan.preparation: Construct an unpopulated Value Proposition Canvas Customer Profile (comprising Jobs, Pains, and Gains) using standardized markdown or digital boards.
plan.execution: Guide users through an unmoderated card-sort protocol. Instruct them to place operational responsibilities into functional, social, and emotional categories, then rank pains by severity and gains by relevance.
plan.dataCollection: Record the spatial clustering of items. Calculate Spearman rank-order correlation coefficients across participant cards.

warning.name: Aspirational Self-Deception
warning.text: Participants consistently overemphasize noble emotional or social jobs while minimizing the mundane, repetitive functional tasks that dictate enterprise purchase behavior.

records.name: Customer Churn and Exit Interview Mining
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that customers abandon [incumbent solution category] because of [deficiency X]. We will verify this by auditing 20 canceled customer accounts or exit interviews, and consider it validated if ≥ 50% identify [deficiency X] as their primary non-negotiable exit driver rather than pricing or budget constraints.

plan.preparation: Extract lists of accounts canceled within the prior 30–60 days. Frame interview outreach as an operational post-mortem aimed at process improvement rather than customer win-back.
plan.execution: Conduct 20-minute structured exit interviews inquiring: "At what specific moment did the product cease delivering anticipated value?" "What workaround did you build prior to cancellation?" "What replacement system was deployed?"
plan.dataCollection: Code exit rationales into root categories: price sensitivity, core product defect, organizational reorganization, or loss of internal champion.

warning.name: Scapegoat Rationalization
warning.text: Churned clients routinely point to price or peripheral software bugs as polite covers rather than acknowledging their organization lacked the operational competence to adopt the platform.

records.name: Public Community and Social Sentiment Mining
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that users of [incumbent software] are actively seeking alternatives due to [specific systemic flaw]. We will verify this by analyzing 300 unresolved negative comments and support threads across industry forums, and consider it validated if ≥ 25% of organic complaint threads focus specifically on [flaw].

plan.preparation: Map primary practitioner communities across specialized forums, GitHub issue trackers, subreddit channels, and professional discussion spaces.
plan.execution: Execute systematic diagnostic search queries using boolean strings (e.g., "how do I fix", "alternative to", "terrible UX", "workaround").
plan.dataCollection: Aggregate complaint structures into an analysis matrix. Track recurring themes, estimated financial losses reported by users, and underlying operational drivers.

warning.name: Selection Bias of Vocal Minorities
warning.text: Public communities amplify the grievances of highly vocal edge-case power users whose requirements diverge significantly from the mainstream market.

records.name: Customer Advisory Board Problem Council
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [industry vertical] executives consider [nascent regulatory or operational challenge] a board-level risk. We will verify this by hosting a 6-executive roundtable, and consider it validated if ≥ 4 members confirm they have formally committed budget to mitigate the issue in the current fiscal year.

plan.preparation: Recruit 6 non-competing industry executives. Frame the session as an off-the-record working council on emerging operational bottlenecks.
plan.execution: Facilitate an executive Chatham House Rule discussion around operational risks. Require each participant to detail their single greatest vulnerability without evaluating potential software solutions.
plan.dataCollection: Record the level of inter-participant validation, specific budget line items disclosed, and shared operational challenges that surface organically across accounts.

warning.name: Executive Echo Chamber
warning.text: Board members often echo high-level industry buzzwords and macro narratives to appear forward-thinking before peers, irrespective of actual internal budget allocation.

records.name: Search Intent and Semantic Volume Reconnaissance
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that consumers are actively searching for ways to solve [problem X]. We will verify this by analyzing search engine queries across targeted keyword groups, and consider it validated if high-intent terms show ≥ 2,500 monthly organic queries with a year-over-year growth rate of ≥ 20%.

plan.preparation: Compile a seed dictionary of high-intent search syntax variants (e.g., "how to automate X", "X alternative", "X compliance template").
plan.execution: Query search volume databases to extract regional search density, historical trajectory, cost-per-click bids, and competitor domain saturation.
plan.dataCollection: Segment search queries into Informational, Navigational, Commercial, and Transactional categories. Calculate the total addressable commercial search volume.

warning.name: Informational Intent Conflation
warning.text: High search volumes for informational queries often signify academic curiosity or individuals looking for free guides, rather than buyers demonstrating commercial intent.

records.name: Critical Incident Technique (CIT) Audit
records.phaseTitle: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [event X] triggers operational failure in [workflow Y]. We will verify this by collecting 15 detailed critical incident reports from practitioners, and consider it validated if ≥ 80% report that the incident caused acute workflow delays, compliance exposure, or direct financial loss.

plan.preparation: Establish explicit inclusion criteria for what constitutes a critical incident (e.g., unscheduled downtime, SLA breach, or emergency executive briefing).
plan.execution: Interview qualified practitioners using the CIT protocol: "Recount the most recent operational failure in your workflow. What specific conditions preceded it? What interventions were deployed, and what systems failed?"
plan.dataCollection: Reconstruct a chronological event map for each incident, detailing the root triggers, secondary compounding effects, and downstream financial costs.

warning.name: Salience and Availability Bias
warning.text: Participants recall dramatic, emotionally charged anomalies with extreme clarity, leading researchers to mistake infrequent operational crises for routine, recurring market needs.

records.name: Desirability, Feasibility, and Viability (DFV) Mapping
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that our cross-functional team holds strategic alignment on our core business vulnerabilities. We will verify this by mapping all operational assumptions across a 2 × 2 matrix (Impact vs. Evidence), and consider it validated if participants achieve ≥ 90% consensus on the top 5 assumptions categorized in the High Impact / Low Evidence quadrant.

plan.preparation: Assemble product, engineering, design, and commercial leaders. Provide each member with assumption tracking cards categorized into Desirability, Feasibility, and Viability.
plan.execution: Instruct members to independently document explicit operational premises. Place every assumption onto a shared 2 × 2 grid: Vertical Axis = Impact (Low vs. High); Horizontal Axis = Current Evidence (Known vs. Unknown).
plan.dataCollection: Cluster overlapping cards into distinct operational themes. Isolate the High Impact / Low Evidence quadrant as the designated experiment backlog.

warning.name: HiPPO Distortion
warning.text: Senior executives frequently drag high-risk assumptions into the "Known" quadrant based entirely on personal conviction, blinding the team to critical structural vulnerabilities.

records.name: Riskiest Assumption Test (RAT) Decomposition
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [Assumption A] represents the single existential bottleneck for the business model. We will verify this by decomposing the business concept into causal dependency trees, and consider it validated if breaking this single assumption mathematically invalidates all downstream unit economics.

plan.preparation: Isolate the top-ranked assumption from the DFV matrix. Break it down into discrete component premises.
plan.execution: Construct a causal dependency tree using "What Must Be True" statements. Trace dependencies backward to identify the foundational premise whose failure collapses the entire structure.
plan.dataCollection: Draft a dedicated testing specification for this root assumption, detailing validation thresholds, temporal boundaries, and required evidence weights.

warning.name: Premature Optimization of Secondary Assumptions
warning.text: Teams frequently expend energy testing easily measurable operational details (such as interface aesthetics or onboarding micro-copy) while sidestepping existential commercial viability risks.

records.name: Problem-Solution Fit Scorecarding
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe our proposed solution addresses the primary pain points discovered in Phase 1. We will verify this by scoring our feature set against validated customer problems using a blind scoring rubric, and consider it validated if ≥ 80% of features map directly to high-severity problems, with all secondary unmapped features eliminated.

plan.preparation: Construct a matrix listing validated customer problems on the vertical axis and proposed feature specifications on the horizontal axis.
plan.execution: Evaluate each intersection: Does this feature directly alleviate this specific problem? Require cross-functional leads to justify each connection with behavioral data gathered in Phase 1.
plan.dataCollection: Calculate the operational coverage ratio. Flag and discard features that solve unvalidated problems or fail to resolve the core bottleneck.

warning.name: Sunk Cost Feature Attachment
warning.text: Product teams routinely construct elaborate post-hoc justifications for favorite features that have no demonstrable link to validated customer problems.

records.name: Stakeholder and Buying Center Influence Mapping (B2B)
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [Role A] controls purchase authority, while [Role B] serves as an internal champion. We will verify this by mapping the buying center dynamics across 8 enterprise target accounts, and consider it validated if the operational economic buyer matches our target persona in ≥ 75% of evaluated org charts.

plan.preparation: Define the six canonical enterprise purchasing roles: Economic Buyer, Champion, End User, Technical Gatekeeper, Procurement, and Blocker.
plan.execution: Conduct organizational discovery calls across multiple departments within each target account. Ask: "Whose departmental budget pays for this solution?" "Who possesses absolute veto authority during procurement and security review?".
plan.dataCollection: Chart the formal decision, veto, and capital authorization pathways for each enterprise account.

warning.name: Champion Conflation
warning.text: Founders routinely mistake an enthusiastic end-user champion for the economic buyer, discovering too late that the deal stalls indefinitely when presented to procurement.

records.name: Value Proposition Fit Matrix (Relievers vs. Pains)
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that our core value proposition outranks existing market alternatives on speed and clarity. We will verify this by presenting a relative comparison matrix to 12 prospective users, and consider it validated if ≥ 70% prioritize our specific pain relievers over incumbent alternatives.

plan.preparation: Build a two-sided Value Proposition Canvas explicitly mapping Pain Relievers to Customer Pains and Gain Creators to Customer Gains.
plan.execution: Conduct structured review sessions where target users evaluate the clarity, relevance, and differentiation of each value proposition element against their current operational alternatives.
plan.dataCollection: Quantify the fit score using a weighted distribution model calibrated to user-prioritized pain points.

warning.name: Theoretical Value Congruence
warning.text: A value proposition can appear conceptually cohesive and compelling on paper while failing to generate sufficient switching momentum to overcome incumbent inertia.

records.name: Reverse-Income Economic Viability Model
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe this business model can achieve sustainable profitability at target scale. We will verify this by building a reverse unit-economics model, and consider it validated if the required conversion rates and average revenue per user (ARPU) remain within historical benchmark ranges for this industry vertical.

plan.preparation: Fix an ambitious financial milestone (e.g., 10,000,000 ARR).
plan.execution: Work backward to calculate the necessary funnel metrics: divide target revenue by expected ARPU to determine the required customer volume, then calculate the necessary conversion rates and acquisition costs across the funnel.
plan.dataCollection: Compare required operational metrics against real-world industry benchmarks: Required Leads = Target ARR / (ARPU × Funnel Conversion Rate)

warning.name: Spreadsheet Viability Syndrome
warning.text: Financial models can always be balanced by inserting aggressive compound growth rates or unrealistically low customer acquisition costs, masking unviable business fundamentals.

records.name: Technical Feasibility Spike and Architecture Proof
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [external API / architecture] can process [X volume] within [Y latency]. We will verify this by deploying an isolated technical spike in a staging environment, and consider it validated if latency remains below 250ms at 1,500 concurrent requests without data loss.

plan.preparation: Strip away all frontend interfaces and non-essential dependencies. Isolate the specific algorithmic or data throughput unknown.
plan.execution: Build a minimal codebase designed solely to stress-test the core integration, algorithm, or data pipeline.
plan.dataCollection: Run automated load scripts, logging latency distributions, memory usage, error codes, and compute costs.

warning.name: Sandbox Isolation Bias
warning.text: A technical architecture that operates smoothly in a clean, isolated staging environment often degrades when exposed to real-world edge cases, dirty legacy data, and unoptimized production dependencies.

records.name: Regulatory and Compliance Gate Audit
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe our proposed data architecture complies fully with relevant regulatory standards (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, SOC2). We will verify this by completing a formal compliance audit with an external specialist, and consider it validated if the audit reveals zero critical regulatory blockers that would require fundamentally altering the product model.

plan.preparation: Document data lifecycles, user consent mechanisms, storage tiers, and cross-border transfer paths.
plan.execution: Walk legal and compliance specialists through the end-to-end data flow to identify regulatory touchpoints.
plan.dataCollection: Log potential legal hurdles, compliance requirements, certification expenses, and expected implementation timelines.

warning.name: Informal Legal Assurances
warning.text: Early-stage teams frequently mistake casual, preliminary guidance from corporate attorneys for formal, binding regulatory clearance.

records.name: Acquisition Channel Scalability Matrix
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [Channel X] can sustainably deliver customer acquisition at targeted unit costs. We will verify this by cross-referencing industry channel benchmarks against product characteristics, and consider it validated if the channel delivers an estimated CAC:LTV ratio of ≥ 1:3 at target market scale.

plan.preparation: Map potential acquisition channels against ARPU tiers and user buying habits.
plan.execution: Eliminate channels that don't match the product's price point (e.g., enterprise direct sales forces are rarely viable for products with an ARPU under $1,000/year).
plan.dataCollection: Build a channel projection matrix comparing expected saturation points, cost-per-click trends, and estimated conversion rates.

warning.name: Channel Mirage Effect
warning.text: Early customer acquisition traction achieved in niche communities or closed groups rarely scales efficiently once broader advertising channels are deployed.

records.name: Van Westendorp Price Sensitivity Meter
records.phaseTitle: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that the acceptable price band for our offering falls between [Price A] and [Price B]. We will verify this by surveying 50 qualified target customers using the four standard Van Westendorp questions, and consider it validated if the Indifference Price Point aligns with our planned market pricing within a ±10% margin.

plan.preparation: Construct a survey detailing the core value proposition. Include the four standard pricing questions: (1) At what price is it too cheap to trust the quality? (2) A bargain? (3) Getting expensive, but still worth considering? (4) Too expensive to consider?
plan.execution: Distribute the instrument strictly to qualified target buyers who match the defined ICP.
plan.dataCollection: Plot cumulative distribution curves to identify the Indifference Price Point (intersection of "Cheap" and "Expensive") and the Optimal Price Point (intersection of "Too Cheap" and "Too Expensive"): Optimal Price Point (OPP) = Intersection of "Too Cheap" and "Too Expensive"

warning.name: Stated Willingness Bias
warning.text: Theoretical pricing surveys reliably overestimate how much customers will actually spend when asked to enter real payment details.

records.name: Fake Door / Ghost Feature Test
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that existing active users need [Feature X]. We will verify this by adding an entry point for the unbuilt feature within our live interface, and consider it validated if ≥ 12% of active users click the link within 7 days, with ≥ 50% opting into an early access notification list.

plan.preparation: Design a native UI element (button, menu entry, or card) for the proposed capability. Build an exit modal explaining: "We are currently finalizing this feature. Join the early access waitlist to get notified when it launches."
plan.execution: Deploy the element to a randomized slice of active users using an open-source feature flag manager.
plan.dataCollection: Track exposures, click-through rates, and opt-in conversions on the explanation modal.

warning.name: Curio-Clicking
warning.text: Users frequently click unexpected buttons simply out of curiosity or novelty, rather than a genuine intent to use the underlying feature.

records.name: Landing Page Smoke Test
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe cold traffic from [Channel A] will convert on [Core Value Proposition]. We will verify this by driving 1,000 qualified visitors to a standalone landing page, and consider it validated if the conversion rate (email capture or pricing tier selection) meets or exceeds 5.0% with a target Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) below $15.00.

plan.preparation: Build a high-converting, single-page website featuring a clear headline, value pillars, social proof, and a prominent primary Call-to-Action (CTA). Configure analytics and tracking events on every button.
plan.execution: Launch targeted paid search or social ad campaigns driving traffic from the target ICP to the landing page.
plan.dataCollection: Track total unique visitors, bounce rate, dwell time, and conversion percentage on the primary CTA.

warning.name: Vanity Email Opt-Ins
warning.text: Visitors will casually provide secondary or burner email addresses to download free materials or peek at a website, with no real intention of purchasing paid software.

records.name: Concierge Minimum Viable Product
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [client segment] will pay for [automated service outcome]. We will verify this by manually delivering the service end-to-end for 5 businesses for three consecutive weeks, and consider it validated if ≥ 4 clients complete the trial and agree to retain the service on a paid monthly basis.

plan.preparation: Define the manual operating workflow, tools, and direct customer communication channels (e.g., Slack, email, shared spreadsheets). Be explicit with the customer that this initial phase involves hands-on white-glove onboarding.
plan.execution: Fulfill the service entirely by hand behind the scenes. Track all human labor hours required to deliver the promised value proposition.
plan.dataCollection: Document customer satisfaction, time spent per unit of delivery, operational edge cases, and client retention rates.

warning.name: White-Glove Bias
warning.text: Customers often stick with the service primarily because they enjoy the direct, highly attentive human consulting, then churn the moment the experience is replaced with self-serve software.

records.name: Wizard of Oz Prototype
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe customers will trust an automated interface to handle [complex task]. We will verify this by building a functioning frontend facade operated entirely by humans on the back end, and consider it validated if users process ≥ 50 transactions with an average Net Promoter Score (NPS) ≥ 50 and an error rate below 5%.

plan.preparation: Build a polished web frontend that mirrors a finished, automated product. Connect form inputs and workflows to internal operational dashboards, alerts, or spreadsheets rather than automated backends.
plan.execution: Deliver the experience in real time using human operators who process incoming requests, pull data manually, and send responses back through the system interface.
plan.dataCollection: Log end-to-end turnaround times, user interaction patterns, system failures, and post-task completion metrics.

warning.name: Unsustainable Fulfillment Expectations
warning.text: Human operators can often resolve confusing edge cases, fix typos, and smooth over bad data in ways that automated code cannot, creating a false impression of product-market fit that breaks down during actual software automation.

records.name: Explainer Video Smoke Test (The Dropbox Prototype)
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe our proposed workflow interface is intuitive enough to drive mass consumer adoption. We will verify this by posting a 2-minute demonstration video showing simulated software interactions to target developer channels, and consider it validated if the waitlist grows by ≥ 10,000 qualified signups within 48 hours.

plan.preparation: Create a short video walking through core product workflows, deliberately highlighting how the product solves acute, relatable user frustrations.
plan.execution: Seed the video across relevant niche communities, developer boards, and technical networks. Link directly to an early access waitlist landing page.
plan.dataCollection: Track video retention drop-off rates, aggregate view counts, landing page conversion percentages, and community discussion tone.

warning.name: Entertainment and Novelty Virality
warning.text: A slick, entertaining, or clever demonstration video can generate significant viral buzz and social shares that fail to translate into active, paying users once the novelty wears off.

records.name: Interactive Paper Prototyping
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that users can navigate our core onboarding flow without training. We will verify this by running 8 paper-prototype usability sessions, and consider it validated if ≥ 7 participants complete the primary conversion path without asking the facilitator for assistance.

plan.preparation: Sketch interface screens, dropdowns, and modals on separate paper index cards. Organize them systematically so a facilitator can swap them in and out quickly.
plan.execution: Give the user a clear task. As they touch the paper buttons with their finger, the facilitator acts as the computer, laying down the corresponding paper modal or screen state.
plan.dataCollection: Note hesitation points, misplaced taps, verbalized confusion, and overall task completion times.

warning.name: Facilitator Coaxing
warning.text: Facilitators often inadvertently guide participants through hesitation points with subtle body language, subconscious nods, or leading prompts, masking interface usability flaws.

records.name: Clickable Wireframe Click-Stream Prototype
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that users can configure their account settings in under 90 seconds. We will verify this by testing an interactive, clickable mock prototype with 15 unassisted target users, and consider it validated if the median Time-to-Complete is under 90 seconds with a task success rate ≥ 80%.

plan.preparation: Build a mid-fidelity clickable prototype in a design tool. Map out realistic click states, input fields, and feedback loops while leaving non-essential branches unclickable.
plan.execution: Distribute the prototype link through an unmoderated testing tool. Ask participants to think out loud as they attempt a specific, structured goal.
plan.dataCollection: Track success paths, misclick heatmaps, total task completion durations, and systemic drop-off steps.

warning.name: Missing Operational Context
warning.text: Users navigating an isolated mockup inside an artificial testing window do not experience the real-world interruptions, messy background data, and technical friction of their actual working environment.

records.name: Crowdfunding Pre-Sales Campaign
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe there is sustained market demand for our hardware/software innovation. We will verify this by launching a 30-day public crowdfunding campaign, and consider it validated if the campaign hits its minimum funding goal of $100,000 from at least 500 individual backers.

plan.preparation: Produce a campaign video, establish production timelines, map out detailed bill-of-materials cost structures, and configure the campaign page and reward tiers.
plan.execution: Launch the campaign publicly and run coordinated promotional campaigns across targeted consumer and industry channels.
plan.dataCollection: Track day-one funding velocity, campaign page conversion rates, backer tier distribution, and average pledge amounts.

warning.name: Early-Adopter Crowdfunding Bubble
warning.text: Crowdfunding platforms attract early adopters and hobbyists who tolerate delays and product bugs; these users rarely reflect the expectations of mainstream mass-market consumers.

records.name: B2B Letter of Intent (LOI) Protocol
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe mid-market enterprises need our proposed integration. We will verify this by presenting a non-binding Letter of Intent (LOI) to 6 prospective enterprise accounts, and consider it validated if at least 2 authorized executives sign the document committing to a paid commercial pilot upon delivery of agreed functional specifications.

plan.preparation: Draft a one-page non-binding Letter of Intent that clearly outlines the business problem, proposed deliverables, expected go-live timeline, and pilot purchase pricing terms.
plan.execution: Present the LOI to the economic buyer once functional requirements have been defined during enterprise sales discussions.
plan.dataCollection: Note points of hesitation, redlines from legal and procurement, and final signature rates.

warning.name: Non-Binding Courtesy Signatures
warning.text: Because standard LOIs are legally non-binding, sympathetic executives will sometimes sign them to encourage early-stage founders or wrap up exploratory calls, only to walk away when asked for formal procurement contracts and budget approvals.

records.name: Refundable Deposit Pre-Order
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe users will pay [Price Y] for our forthcoming product. We will verify this by running a pre-order campaign with a required, refundable $50 reservation deposit, and consider it validated if ≥ 3.0% of unique page visitors complete the checkout transaction.

plan.preparation: Build a checkout flow that clearly states the product is in active development, offering priority queue placement in exchange for a refundable deposit.
plan.execution: Drive qualified traffic to the reservation page and process real financial transactions via a payment gateway.
plan.dataCollection: Measure payment completion rates, refund requests, and customer questions submitted during checkout.

warning.name: Frictionless Refund Psychology
warning.text: When deposits are low, fully refundable, and clearly framed as risk-free, conversion rates often artificially inflate, as buyers treat the checkout as an easy way to bookmark the product rather than an actual purchase commitment.

records.name: Micro-Ad Engagement Funnel Siphon
records.phaseTitle: Low-Fidelity Prototyping and Smoke Testing Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [Value Proposition Messaging A] resonates more strongly with consumers than [Messaging B]. We will verify this by running split ad campaigns with equal budget allocations across both messages, and consider it validated if Variant A yields a ≥ 40% higher Click-Through Rate (CTR) and ≥ 25% lower Cost Per Click (CPC) at statistical significance (p < 0.05).

plan.preparation: Create identical graphic assets that differ only in their core headline and copy hooks (e.g., Cost Savings vs. Time Savings).
plan.execution: Launch simultaneous ad sets on a single acquisition platform targeting an identical audience segment. Set daily spending caps to avoid skewing data.
plan.dataCollection: Track impressions, clicks, CTR, and downstream page engagement metrics across each creative variant.

warning.name: Clickbait Disconnection
warning.text: Sensationalist or curiosity-driven ad copy can achieve high click-through rates and low acquisition costs while attracting visitors who bounce immediately once they land on the actual product page.

records.name: Pirate Metrics (AARRR) Baseline Funnel Audit
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that our product funnel converts prospects efficiently from initial discovery through to paid renewal. We will verify this by instrumenting end-to-end event telemetry across all five funnel stages, and consider it validated if we achieve baseline conversions of ≥ 20% Acquisition-to-Activation and ≥ 5% Activation-to-Revenue.

plan.preparation: Define operational metrics for each funnel step: Acquisition (unique landing visitor), Activation (core value moment reached), Retention (return usage within 7 days), Revenue (payment executed), and Referral (invite dispatched).
plan.execution: Instrument analytics events for each operational step using an open-source product analytics or data warehouse platform.
plan.dataCollection: Build a conversion funnel visualization, tracking conversion percentages and user velocity between successive steps.

warning.name: Blended Funnel Distortions
warning.text: Evaluating the funnel as a single, blended average hides performance differences across individual traffic channels, masking the fact that poor paid traffic is diluting strong organic engagement.

records.name: Cohort Retention Decay Curve Analysis
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that our product delivers sustained, long-term utility to users. We will verify this by tracking weekly active usage across monthly cohorts, and consider it validated if the retention curve flattens into a stable horizontal asymptote at ≥ 20% weekly active retention by Week 8: lim R(t) as t → ∞  ≥ 0.20

plan.preparation: Define the core engagement action that reflects genuine product value (e.g., exporting a project or collaborating with a teammate), rather than simply logging in.
plan.execution: Group users into discrete cohorts based on the calendar week or month they completed onboarding. Track their activity over time.
plan.dataCollection: Plot percentage retention curves for each cohort over time, tracking whether the retention trajectory flattens or continues decaying toward the origin.

warning.name: The Walking Dead Metric Trap
warning.text: A company can show impressive top-line growth in total registered users while its underlying cohort retention curves decay steadily to zero, meaning growth will stall the moment acquisition spend slows.

records.name: Sean Ellis PMF Survey Engine (The 40% Rule)
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe our product has achieved early product-market fit within its core user segment. We will verify this by surveying users who have experienced the core product at least twice in the past fortnight, and consider it validated if ≥ 40% state they would be "very disappointed" if the product disappeared tomorrow.

plan.preparation: Build a short survey centered on the question: "How would you feel if you could no longer use [Product]?" with four fixed responses: (a) Very disappointed, (b) Somewhat disappointed, (c) Not disappointed, or (d) I no longer use it.
plan.execution: Send the survey exclusively to users who have completed the onboarding flow and engaged with the product multiple times.
plan.dataCollection: Calculate the proportion of respondents who choose "Very disappointed." Segment these responses by user demographic and persona to isolate where satisfaction is strongest: PMF Score = Count("Very Disappointed") / Total Qualified Respondents × 100 ≥ 40%

warning.name: Surveying Casual, Non-Core Users
warning.text: Sending the survey to all registered users—including those who signed up and immediately bounced—dilutes the score and obscures product-market fit within the true target segment.

records.name: Net Promoter Score and Root-Cause Decomposition
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that users advocate organically for our product. We will verify this by running an in-app Net Promoter survey with open-ended follow-up prompts, and consider it validated if the overall score meets or exceeds +40, with ≥ 50% of Promoters pointing to the same core capability as their primary reason for recommending it.

plan.preparation: Add a standard 0–10 NPS rating prompt to the product interface, triggered only after a user successfully completes a core milestone.
plan.execution: Group responses into Promoters (9–10), Passives (7–8), and Detractors (0–6). For all scores, trigger an immediate open-ended follow-up asking for the specific reason behind the rating.
plan.dataCollection: Calculate the overall score: NPS = % Promoters − % Detractors

warning.name: Passive Satisfaction Inflation
warning.text: Teams often treat high proportions of Passive respondents (ratings of 7 or 8) as evidence of product health, ignoring that these users regularly switch when a competitor offers lower pricing or better features.

records.name: Feature-Flagged Canary Experiment
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [Redesigned Workflow X] increases task completion rates compared to the current baseline. We will verify this by deploying the redesign to 10% of production traffic via an open-source feature flag, and consider it validated if the treatment group shows a statistically significant lift in task completions (≥ 15%, p < 0.05) without degrading error rates or latency.

plan.preparation: Instrument the alternative workflow behind a dynamic feature flag rule, defining exposure keys and logging attributes.
plan.execution: Route a randomized 10% traffic split to the variant while monitoring error logs and system health. Gradually increase traffic to 50% as system stability is confirmed.
plan.dataCollection: Track conversion rates, system errors, operational latency, and task completion times across both control and treatment variations.

warning.name: Early Peeking and Underpowered Samples
warning.text: Stopping an experiment early the moment a p-value dips below 0.05 dramatically increases the rate of false positives; sample sizes and experiment durations must be locked in advance.

records.name: Unit Economics Stress Test (CAC:LTV Ratio)
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe our customer acquisition model is economically sustainable. We will verify this by measuring blended and paid Customer Acquisition Costs alongside early cohort churn and revenue, and consider it validated if the projected Lifetime Value to Customer Acquisition Cost ratio exceeds 3:1, with full CAC payback achieved in ≤ 12 months: LTV / CAC ≥ 3.0, where LTV = (ARPU × Gross Margin) / Churn Rate

plan.preparation: Aggregate all fully loaded acquisition costs (ad spend, sales commissions, operational overhead, marketing software) across a 60-day testing window.
plan.execution: Track the total number of paid customer accounts generated specifically from those spend allocations.
plan.dataCollection: Calculate the months required to recover customer acquisition costs: Payback Period (Months) = CAC / (ARPU × Gross Margin %)

warning.name: Blended CAC Smuggling
warning.text: Blending cheap organic, direct, or personal network traffic with paid marketing spend obscures high paid customer acquisition costs, hiding an unviable acquisition channel.

records.name: Minimum Viable Experiment (MVE) Timeboxing
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe we can determine whether to pursue [Hypothesis X] in five business days. We will verify this by running a structured, strictly timeboxed five-day testing sprint, and consider it validated if the team gathers enough behavioral data to pass an agreed quantitative validation gate by Day 5.

plan.preparation: On Monday morning, isolate a single critical unknown. Design an experiment whose asset preparation, user exposure, and data analysis can complete inside one business week.
plan.execution: Run asset preparation on Monday and Tuesday, deploy the test to live traffic on Wednesday and Thursday, and close data collection on Friday at midday.
plan.dataCollection: Present the raw results during a Friday retrospective, enforcing an immediate decision: Validate, Invalidate, or Kill.

warning.name: Sunk Cost Rationalization Extensions
warning.text: Teams often extend testing deadlines when initial results are ambiguous or discouraging, hoping that running the test a few days longer will salvage their favored hypothesis.

records.name: Micro-Conversion Step Drop-Off Audit
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that [Step 3 in our onboarding flow] causes unnecessary user drop-off. We will verify this by instrumenting telemetry across every form field and screen transition, and consider it validated if simplifying that single step reduces drop-off by ≥ 30% without lowering downstream activation quality.

plan.preparation: Map every user input field, click, and screen transition in the target path into a sequential funnel model.
plan.execution: Log drop-off percentages, validation errors, and interaction times for every field across 500 user sessions.
plan.dataCollection: Plot the drop-off gradient across each micro-step to identify points of user friction.

warning.name: Removing Essential Friction
warning.text: Streamlining onboarding forms by cutting out identity checks or qualification questions can boost completion rates while flooding the product with unqualified or spam accounts.

records.name: Paid Pilot Milestone Contract Verification
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe enterprises will pay for our complete workflow solution. We will verify this by executing 3 paid commercial pilot agreements with explicit performance milestones, and consider it validated if at least 2 enterprise accounts meet their operational criteria and convert to multi-year contracts upon completion.

plan.preparation: Draft a commercial pilot agreement specifying target operational milestones, integration timelines, and auto-converting production pricing terms.
plan.execution: Deploy the system inside the enterprise environment, providing operational support to ensure the team hits the agreed performance milestones.
plan.dataCollection: Track progress against the contractually agreed metrics and record conversion rates to multi-year production licenses.

warning.name: Perpetual Pilot Trap
warning.text: Enterprise buyers sometimes use low-cost innovation pilots to run exploratory tests or satisfy internal innovation quotas without intending to secure broad organizational rollout.

records.name: Referral Engine and Viral Coefficient (K-factor) Test
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe that our product includes natural referral loops that drive organic growth. We will verify this by adding an in-product referral mechanism to active user workflows, and consider it validated if the measured Viral Coefficient (K) exceeds 0.40: K = i × c where i represents invitations sent per active user, and c represents the conversion rate per invitation.

plan.preparation: Build a frictionless referral touchpoint integrated directly into the core product value loop (e.g., inviting a collaborator to view or edit a document), rather than a generic marketing invite button.
plan.execution: Track invitation generation rates, link shares, and new user signups across 300 active users.
plan.dataCollection: Calculate the viral loop variables over time, tracking the cycle time elapsed between a user signing up and their invited referee joining the platform.

warning.name: Artificial Incentive Distortion
warning.text: Offering high cash or credit rewards can drive high volumes of spam invites, inflating short-term viral numbers with users who bounce immediately after collecting the reward.

records.name: Formal Pivot vs. Persevere Evaluation
records.phaseTitle: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
records.hypothesis: We believe our recent experimentation results provide sufficient empirical evidence to guide our next strategic product cycle. We will verify this by evaluating our cumulative testing metrics against predetermined milestone gates, and consider it validated if the cross-functional leadership team reaches unanimous consensus on an operational path forward (Persevere, Pivot, or Terminate).

plan.preparation: Consolidate quantitative findings from all completed testing cards across Phases 1 through 4. Synthesize the findings into an objective, factual memo that highlights failures and disconfirmed assumptions without spin.
plan.execution: Convene an innovation review board. Evaluate current progress against the three canonical options: Persevere (core hypotheses validated; scale execution), Pivot (fundamental premise disproven, but discovery surfaced an adjacent high-urgency friction point), or Terminate (core premises invalidated with no viable adjacent opportunities; reallocate capital).
plan.dataCollection: Document the strategic decision, supporting evidence, and resource reallocations in a permanent decision record.

warning.name: Sunk Cost Fallacy and Identity Entanglement
warning.text: Teams regularly choose to persevere with flawed, disproven ideas because they conflate admitting a hypothesis failed with personal or professional failure, burning remaining capital on unproductive work.
